_comment: Copy to inbox/harness.json and edit. Config for the daily evaluation harness (bidkit.harness + bidkit.digest), run by bin/bid-harness.sh. Paths are relative to the bidkit/ working directory (that is where the modules run), matching the other inbox configs. NO SECRETS HERE: the digest recipient is config, but the Gmail SEND credentials live in secrets/ (send_token_file) just like the fetch token.
_autonomy: a = notify-only (DEFAULT; evaluate + email, never write) | b = quarantine (agent writes to opportunities/<id>/<quarantine_dir>/, a human promotes) | c = full (agent writes canonical docs, gated only by the gates). Mode is config, never code. Start at 'a'; move to 'b' only once a headless agent runner exists and the gates have earned trust.
_agent_cli: Path/command of a headless agent runner for modes b/c. null = none available → the harness degrades to notify-only and says so. There is no headless agent CLI on this box yet, so leave null for now.
_ingest: The harness does NOT poll mail itself; bin/bid-inbox.sh and bin/bid-source.sh run first and file opportunities. Left here as a flag for a future combined entry point.

digest._comment: The daily email. 'to' is the principal; 'org_name' is only used in the lead line/subject (kept out of library code). 'send_on_empty': false suppresses the email on a quiet day (nothing added/updated). Drafts larger than max_attachment_mb are linked by path instead of attached.
digest._gmail_api: Reuses the Gmail SEND path (bidkit.mail_gmail.send_raw). The send scope needs its own one-time consent and token, separate from the read-only fetch token: cd bidkit && python3 -m bidkit.mail_gmail send-auth --cfg ../inbox/inbox.json . send_token_file defaults to ../secrets/gmail-send-token.json.
